newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan newspaper says Eritrea behind attack.
newsitem.headline: Sudan newspaper says Eritrea behind attack.

text.p: An Eritrean army captain has surrendered to the Sudanese army and told his captors Eritrean troops were behind a recent attack on northeast Sudan, a newspaper said on Sunday.
The privately-owned Alwan said Abdel-Gadir Ali Younis, 36, surrendered to "our (Sudanese) forces at the eastern border because he was not convinced with the reasons for the war on Sudan".
"The forces that took part in the latest attack on Togan were 100 percent Eritrean," the paper quoted Younis as saying.

Khartoum's Islamist government has accused Eritrea, Ethiopia and Uganda of fighting alongside northern and southern rebels to overthrow President Omar Hassan al-Bashir. All three countries deny the charge.
A rebel coalition under the command of Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) leader John Garang has said it is behind the fighting in Sudan's northeast and southern areas.
